beats.text: Genuinely and measurably radioactive, not a trace amount you need instruments to notice in principle.
beats.note: The radioactivity comes from potassium-40, a naturally occurring isotope that makes up a small fraction of all the potassium in a banana, and in you.

beats.context: how many you would need to eat in a single day just to match an average day's ordinary background radiation exposure.

beats.text: Potassium-40 has been decaying since before the Earth finished forming: its half-life is about 1.25 billion years.
beats.note: It is the largest source of natural internal radioactivity in the human body, not an exotic contamination.

beats.text: Eating more bananas does not raise your radiation dose the way repeated exposure normally would.
beats.note: The body keeps potassium levels roughly constant. Any extra is cleared out within hours, which is also why physicists call 'banana equivalent dose' a flawed unit rather than a real measurement.

beats.text: You are also radioactive. So is the banana. Neither of you should worry about it.
